title: Electric excitation of spin resonance in altermagnetic and antiferromagnetic conductors
authors: R. Ramazashvili, V. Shablenko, Ya. B. Bazaliy
abstract: We predict electric-dipole spin resonance (EDSR) in altermagnetic conductors: in a magnetic field ${\mathbf H}_\perp$, perpendicular to the magnetization axis, an AC electric field will induce a \textit{spin} resonance peak above the lower threshold frequency $ω_- = 2H_\perp$. In sufficiently clean samples, this peak shall be clearly visible on the background of ohmic absorption. EDSR can thus serve as a diagnostic of altermagnetism in conducting materials and as a means to distinguish it from higher-symmetry antiferromagnetic order.
summary: This theoretical work predicts that altermagnetic conductors exhibit a unique Electric-Dipole Spin Resonance (EDSR) peak when subjected to an AC electric field perpendicular to the magnetization. This resonance occurs above a threshold frequency determined by the transverse magnetic field, offering a powerful method to experimentally distinguish altermagnetism from conventional antiferromagnetism.
main_problem: The paper aims to predict and provide a diagnostic signature for Electric-Dipole Spin Resonance (EDSR) in altermagnetic and antiferromagnetic conductors, allowing differentiation from other magnetic orders.
main_result: EDSR manifests as a distinct spin resonance peak above a lower threshold frequency $\omega_- = 2H_\perp/\hbar$, which can serve as a unique diagnostic tool for altermagnetism.
method: The analysis uses a combination of kinetic equation treatments and diagrammatic calculations within the Matsubara formalism to derive the spin polarization and absorption rate.
model_or_system: The system involves altermagnetic and antiferromagnetic conductors, modeled using a low-energy Hamiltonian incorporating spontaneous spin splitting ($\Delta_p$) and an external transverse magnetic field ($\mathbf{H}_\perp$).
key_observables: The primary observable is the EDSR absorption rate ($P_{s\omega}$), which is compared against the background ohmic absorption ($P_{e\omega}$).
important_parameters: Key parameters include the transverse magnetic field $H_\perp$, the ratio $m/M$ characterizing spin splitting, and the clean limit condition $k_F l \approx 2\mu	au \gtrsim 300$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the relaxation-time approximation for the spin polarization and assumes that vertex corrections vanish for $\delta$-correlated disorder.

Figure 2 shows the evolution of the total absorption $P(\omega)$ with increasing magnetic field, and Figure 3 details the diagrammatic calculation framework.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model and Hamiltonian, derives the EDSR signal using kinetic equations and diagrammatic methods, predicts the characteristic frequency thresholds ($\omega_-$), and discusses the experimental conditions required for clear observation.
why_interesting: The theoretical framework for EDSR provides a concrete, measurable spectroscopic signature related to magnetic order, which is highly relevant for understanding exotic electronic states in correlated materials.
